items.title: Groupoids in schemes, relations and etale equivalence relations
items.statement: A groupoid in $S$-schemes is a tuple $(U,R,s,t,c,e,i)$ of $S$-schemes and morphisms $s,t\colon R\to U$ (source and target), $c\colon R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ (composition), $e\colon U\to R$ (identity) and $i\colon R\to R$ (inverse) satisfying the usual identities of a small groupoid ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]], [[def-scheme-over-base]]). With $j=(t,s)\colon R\to U\times_SU$, the groupoid is a relation when $j$ is a monomorphism ([[def-monomorphism-and-epimorphism]]); then $j$ presents $R$ as a reflexive, symmetric and transitive set-theoretic relation on $U$. An equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ is a groupoid in $S$-schemes that is a relation. It is an etale equivalence relation when in addition $s$ and $t$ are etale ([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]). For a morphism of $S$-schemes $g\colon U'\to U$ the restriction $R'=R|_{U'}$ is the base change $R\times_{s,U}U'$ with source and target the two projections, equipped with the base-changed groupoid structure; restricting an equivalence relation gives an equivalence relation ([[def-equivalence-relation]] gives the underlying set-theoretic notion).
items.strategy: Definition and well-definedness checks following Stacks, *Groupoids*, Definition 39.3.1, Lemma 39.3.2 and Definition 39.9.1 (tags 022P, 022Q), and Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Definition 65.9.2 (tag 02WS) for the etale case. A monomorphism $j\colon R\to U\times_SU$ encodes a subfunctor of $U\times_SU$, and the maps $s,t,c,e,i$ encode the relation operations and their axioms; the groupoid axioms are the usual commutativity of the standard diagrams. Vistoli Sections 3.4 and 3.5 give the same structure in fibred-category language. Etale morphisms are stable under base change (published [[lem-etale-stable-base-change-composition]]), so restrictions of etale equivalence relations are etale equivalence relations; this is recorded separately as [[lem-etale-equivalence-relation-restriction]].

items.title: Restriction of an etale equivalence relation
items.statement: Let $j\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]) and let $g\colon U'\to U$ be a morphism of $S$-schemes. Form the restriction $R'=R|_{U'}=R\times_{s,U}U'$ with source and target the standard projections ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). Then $j'\colon R'\to U'\times_SU'$ is an equivalence relation on $U'$ over $S$; if $g$ is etale, then $j'$ is an etale equivalence relation. The source and target of $R'$ are base changes of $s$ and $t$ along $g$, hence etale whenever $g$ and $s,t$ are.
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Groupoids*, Lemma 39.18.1 and *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.10.1 (tag 02WT), read in full. The composition, identity, inverse and monomorphism property of the restricted groupoid are obtained by base change from those of $R$; the source $s'$ and target $t'$ are compositions of base changes of $s,t$, hence etale by the published stability lemma [[lem-etale-stable-base-change-composition]]. No separation or finiteness hypotheses are used.

items.title: Base change of the quotient sheaf along a flat locally finitely presented map
items.statement: Let $s,t\colon R\to U$ be an equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]) such that $s$ and $t$ are flat ([[def-flat-morphism-schemes]]) and locally of finite presentation ([[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]). Let $g\colon U'\to U$ be flat and locally of finite presentation, and let $R'=R|_{U'}$ be the restriction ([[lem-etale-equivalence-relation-restriction]]). Then the canonical morphism of fppf quotient sheaves $U'/R'\to U/R$ ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]) is an isomorphism. In particular, for such relations the quotient sheaf commutes with flat locally finitely presented base change on $U$, and the map $U'/R'\to U/R$ is surjective.
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.10.2 (tag 02WU), read in full. A section of $U/R$ over $T$ is represented fppf-locally by a section of $U$; since $g$ is flat and locally of finite presentation it is an fppf covering onto its open image, and the two maps $s,t$ being flat and locally of finite presentation make the relation fppf-local, so local lifts along $g$ can be chosen and any two differ by a section of $R$ lying fppf-locally in $R'$. The plus-construction description of the quotient sheaf ([[lem-fppf-sheafification-exists]]) converts these local statements into the isomorphism of sheaves. Stability of flat locally finitely presented morphisms under base change is the published [[lem-flat-morphisms-stable-base-change]].

items.title: Effective fppf descent for separated locally quasi-finite morphisms
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $\{X_i\to X\}$ be an fppf covering of an $S$-scheme $X$ ([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]). If $(V_i/X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is a descent datum for schemes ([[def-descent-data-for-schemes]]) and each $V_i\to X_i$ is separated ([[def-separated-morphism-schemes]]) and locally quasi-finite ([[def-quasi-finite-morphism-schemes]]), then the descent datum is effective: there is a scheme $V\to X$, separated and locally quasi-finite over $X$, with compatible isomorphisms $V\times_XX_i\cong V_i$.
items.strategy: Transcription of Stacks, *More on Morphisms*, Lemma 37.57.1 (tag 02W8), whose complete proof is in the source (Section 37.57, *Descending separated locally quasi-finite morphisms*). Route: (1) reduce to a single flat surjective finitely presented affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ using the formal reduction of Stacks 35.36.2; (2) for a descent datum $(V,\varphi)$ with $V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ separated and locally quasi-finite, glue the affine charts of $V$ using the closed graphs of the transition isomorphisms, local quasi-finiteness providing open neighbourhoods in the relevant fibre products and separatedness providing uniqueness; (3) separatedness and local quasi-finiteness of the glued morphism are checked on the cover. The result is due to Raynaud-Gruson Lemma 5.7.1; equivalent statements occur in Murre and SGA 3 Expose X Lemma 5.4 under local finite presentation. No choice principle is used; the proof is constructive from the descent datum.

items.title: Quotient maps of etale equivalence relations are etale surjective
items.statement: Let $j=(s,t)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on an $S$-scheme $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]) and let $F=U/R$ be its fppf quotient sheaf ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]). If $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]), then the canonical morphism $c\colon U\to F$ is representable, etale and surjective; hence $(U,R,U\to F)$ is a presentation of $F$ ([[def-presentation-of-an-algebraic-space]]).
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.10.3 (tag 02WV), read in full. For $T\to F$, representability of $T\times_FU$ is checked after an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$: on $T_i$ the fibre product is $T_i\times_{a_i,U,t}R$ for suitable $a_i$ (existence uses the plus-construction description of the quotient sheaf), which is representable and etale over $T_i$ because $t$ is etale; the resulting descent datum for a separated locally quasi-finite morphism is effective by [[lem-effective-fppf-descent-separated-locally-quasi-finite]], so $T\times_FU$ is representable by a scheme. Etaleness and surjectivity then follow by base change, and the presentation statement is the definition. The existence of the local maps $a_i$ is the same argument as in [[lem-quotient-sheaf-base-change-along-flat-lfp-map]].

items.title: The quotient of an affine etale equivalence relation is an algebraic space
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, let $U$ be an affine $S$-scheme and let $j=(s,t)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]). Then the fppf quotient sheaf $F=U/R$ ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]) is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]) and $U\to F$ is representable, etale and surjective.
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.10.4 (tag 0265), read in full. Step 1: $j$ is a monomorphism, hence separated; $U$ affine makes $U\times_SU$ separated and $R$ separated; $s,t$ are separated etale, the composition $R\to U\times_SU\to U$ is locally of finite type, so $j$ is locally of finite type and, being a monomorphism, locally quasi-finite. Step 2: representability of $c\colon U\to F$: for $T\to F$ choose an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and $a_i\colon T_i\to U$ as in the proofs of [[lem-quotient-sheaf-base-change-along-flat-lfp-map]] and [[lem-quotient-map-etale-when-quotient-is-algebraic-space]]; then $T_i\times_T(T\times_FU)\cong T_i\times_{a_i,U,t}R$, separated and locally quasi-finite over $T_i$, and the descent datum is effective by [[lem-effective-fppf-descent-separated-locally-quasi-finite]]. Step 3: etaleness and surjectivity of $U\to F$ follow since its base changes are base changes of the etale surjective $t$. Step 4: representability of the diagonal $F\to F\times F$: the square with $R\to U\times_SU$ and the diagonal is cartesian, $U\times_SU\to F\times F$ is representable etale surjective, and representability is fppf-local on the target, again by effectivity of descent for separated locally quasi-finite morphisms (the maps involved are etale). The affine hypothesis is used only in Step 1 to obtain separatedness of $U\times_SU$ and $R$.

items.title: Quotients of schemes by etale equivalence relations are algebraic spaces
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, let $U$ be an $S$-scheme and let $j=(s,t)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]). Then the fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$ ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]) is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]), and $U\to U/R$ is representable, etale and surjective; consequently $(U,R,U\to U/R)$ is a presentation of $U/R$ ([[def-presentation-of-an-algebraic-space]]).
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Theorem 65.10.5 (tag 02WW), read in full. Steps: (1) by [[lem-quotient-map-etale-when-quotient-is-algebraic-space]] it suffices to prove that $U/R$ is an algebraic space; (2) replacing $U$ by a surjective etale cover $U'\to U$ does not change the quotient: the restriction $R'=R|_{U'}$ is an etale equivalence relation by [[lem-etale-equivalence-relation-restriction]] and $U/R\cong U'/R'$ by [[lem-quotient-sheaf-base-change-along-flat-lfp-map]]; choosing $U'=\coprod_iU_i$ with $U_i$ affine open reduces to the case where $U$ is a disjoint union of affine schemes; (3) for each $i$ the restriction $R_i$ is an etale equivalence relation, $F_i=U_i/R_i$ is an algebraic space with $U_i\to F_i$ etale surjective by [[lem-affine-etale-equivalence-relation-quotient]], and the induced maps $F_i\to F$ are representable open immersions with $\coprod_iF_i\to F$ surjective ([[lem-quotient-sheaf-base-change-along-flat-lfp-map]]); (4) $\coprod_iF_i$ is an algebraic space (part (1) of [[lem-open-immersion-gluing-of-algebraic-spaces]] with the covers $U_i$) and all hypotheses of part (2) hold, so $F$ is an algebraic space; (5) $U\to U/R$ is representable etale surjective by [[lem-quotient-map-etale-when-quotient-is-algebraic-space]], and the presentation statement is the definition.
